title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of quantum states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines a class of tensors called tight connectors and shows how contracting them according to a renormalization group scheme yields tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities.
result: The constructed inequalities are tight and enable self-testing of multipartite quantum states, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: Provides a systematic method to generate multipartite quantum Bell inequalities, advancing the study of multipartite nonlocality and self-testing.

title: Advantage Of Flexible Catalysis For Entanglement And Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, and Alexander Streltsov

Understanding the fundamental limits of state convertibility is crucial for establishing the boundaries of quantum information processing and thermodynamic efficiency. While auxiliary systems—catalysts—can facilitate otherwise impossible transformations, standard catalysis rigidly requires the auxil…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022407] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces flexible catalysts that can be used in multiple copies, showing they provide an advantage over rigid catalysts for entanglement and quantum thermodynamics state conversions.
motivation: Standard catalysis in quantum resource theories requires the catalyst to be returned unchanged, which may be too restrictive. The authors aim to explore whether allowing the catalyst to be used flexibly (e.g., in multiple copies) can expand the set of achievable transformations.
method: The authors formalize the concept of flexible catalysts, where the catalyst can be used in multiple copies or with some tolerance, and analyze state convertibility under these conditions for entanglement and thermodynamic settings.
result: They demonstrate that flexible catalysis enables otherwise impossible transformations, providing an advantage over rigid catalysis in both entanglement theory and quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: Flexible catalysis is a powerful resource that broadens the boundaries of state convertibility, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamic efficiency.

title: Probing An Electron-spin Ensemble With Squeezed Microwave Signals
authors: P. Oehrl, F. Fesquet, K. E. Honasoge, M. Handschuh, A. Marx, R. Gross, K. G. Fedorov, And H. Huebl
abstract:
Author(s): P. Oehrl, F. Fesquet, K. E. Honasoge, M. Handschuh, A. Marx, R. Gross, K. G. Fedorov, and H. Huebl

The efficient transfer of quantum states into a long-lived storage unit such as solid-state spin ensembles is widely recognized as a critical challenge with significant implications for quantum communication, sensing, and computing applications. Here, we experimentally investigate the interaction of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022603] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes an electron-spin ensemble using squeezed microwave signals, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity and quantum state transfer capabilities.
motivation: Efficient transfer of quantum states into long-lived solid-state spin ensembles is critical for quantum communication, sensing, and computing. Probing such ensembles with squeezed light can improve measurement sensitivity and enable quantum-enhanced protocols.
method: The authors use a superconducting circuit to generate squeezed microwave signals and interact them with an electron-spin ensemble (e.g., NV centers or similar). They measure the reflected/transmitted signals to characterize the spin ensemble's response and coherence.
result: They observe enhanced signal-to-noise ratio and demonstrate the ability to probe the spin ensemble with reduced noise, indicating improved sensitivity and potential for quantum state transfer.
conclusion: The work showcases a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems, combining superconducting circuits with spin ensembles for quantum networking and sensing applications.

title: Scalable Repeater Architecture For Long-range Quantum Energy Teleportation In Gapped Systems
authors: M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Irfan Siddique, Saeed Haddadi, And Cong-Feng Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Irfan Siddique, Saeed Haddadi, and Cong-Feng Qiao

Quantum Energy Teleportation (QET) is a protocol in which a remote measurement activates locally inaccessible ergotropy stored in the ground state of a many-body system by consuming preexisting entanglement and a classical communication channel. Nevertheless, the implementation of QET is severely im…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable repeater architecture for quantum energy teleportation in gapped systems, addressing the practical limitation of short teleportation distances.
motivation: Quantum energy teleportation (QET) is limited by the need for long-distance entanglement distribution, which is challenging in gapped systems. The authors aim to overcome this by designing a repeater-based architecture.
method: The authors introduce a scalable repeater scheme that uses entanglement swapping and purification to extend the range of QET, and analyze its performance in terms of teleported energy and fidelity.
result: The proposed architecture enables long-range QET with improved energy transfer efficiency and scalability, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for implementing QET over long distances, which is a significant step towards quantum energy technologies.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum repeater scheme using GKP qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, integrating quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires quantum repeaters to overcome loss and noise. Existing schemes often rely on either entanglement swapping or error correction, but combining both on flying and stationary qubits could improve performance.
method: The authors design a repeater architecture where GKP qudits are used for both photonic (flying) and matter (stationary) qubits, implementing quantum error correction at each node to correct errors during transmission and storage.
result: The scheme demonstrates improved entanglement distribution rates and resilience to loss compared to previous approaches, with numerical simulations showing enhanced performance.
conclusion: The proposed GKP-based repeater offers a promising path toward practical long-distance quantum networks by integrating error correction into both flying and stationary components.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously without active feedback.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, effectively creating a squeezed environment that stabilizes the entanglement. The technique mimics a squeezed environment to protect the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement between separate devices, demonstrating that the stabilization technique maintains the quantum connection even with real-world imperfections.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for autonomous entanglement stabilization in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two distant superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum network entanglement distribution.
motivation: Distributing entanglement between distant stationary qubits is crucial for quantum networks, but existing methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A passive, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a scalable and robust solution.
method: The authors couple two spatially separated superconducting qubits to a common microwave resonator that is driven into a squeezed state, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the nonlocal correlations of the squeezed light mediate entanglement between them.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the generation of stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with the entanglement persisting as long as the squeezing is maintained. The process is autonomous, requiring no active feedback or measurement.
conclusion: This work establishes a new paradigm for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, leveraging squeezed reservoirs to passively entangle distant qubits, which could enhance the scalability and robustness of future quantum communication systems.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler approach using non-Abelian anyons.
method: The method involves temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, leveraging the properties of non-Abelian anyons for computation.
result: The paper demonstrates a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for intricate braiding, potentially simplifying hardware requirements.
conclusion: This work advances the field of quantum error correction and fault tolerance, offering a new theoretical framework that could impact practical quantum computing architectures.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have quantum emitters with strong light-matter interaction, quantified by coherent cooperativity above unity.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy (SnV) centers to them, measuring the cavity-enhanced emission and coherent cooperativity.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, demonstrating strong coupling between the SnV centers and the cavity mode, which is a key requirement for efficient spin-photon entanglement.
conclusion: This work establishes SnV centers in diamond cavities as a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation and quantum repeaters.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a unified criterion for quantumness in individual processes, addressing inconsistencies in existing signatures and uncovering nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process theories and generalized probabilistic theories, defining a notion of nonclassicality for individual processes and analyzing various examples.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures while showing that many phenomena thought classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties, with potential technological implications.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum-classical boundary and suggests new avenues for exploiting nonclassicality in quantum information processing.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but traditional readout methods suffer from Purcell decay and trade-offs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors design a readout scheme exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive shift while suppressing Purcell decay through a bandgap or filtering effect.
result: They demonstrate fast readout with high fidelity and reduced Purcell decay, improving the performance of transmon qubits.
conclusion: This architecture offers a promising solution for high-performance qubit readout, advancing the practical implementation of superconducting quantum processors.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, improving upon previous methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a practical path towards scalable quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating non-projective measurements by projective ones, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete framework for such certification.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective measurements, and demonstrate it experimentally using a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous and complete certification method, and the experimental demonstration confirms its practical applicability on a real quantum platform.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum measurements and offers a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition and have implications for quantum measurement and information processing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and processors requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which are challenging due to spectral diffusion and individual addressing.
method: The authors propose a control framework that leverages global driving and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, using techniques to mitigate inhomogeneity.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation with reduced experimental overhead, demonstrated for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum information processing with solid-state spin ensembles, relevant for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic applications, but existing implementations often rely on trusted devices. Self-testing protocols offer device-independent security, yet they are typically complex and bulky, hindering practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, integrating all necessary optical components on a single chip.
result: The chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing capabilities, demonstrating the feasibility of miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, compact, and secure quantum random number generators, bridging the gap between theoretical device-independent protocols and real-world applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is limited by resource overhead and loss. Efficient tree-code generation and geometry optimization can improve repeater efficiency and practicality.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation scheme for quantum tree codes and introduce optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through analytical modeling and numerical simulations.
result: The combined approach boosts quantum repeater performance, reducing resource requirements and improving loss tolerance, making repeaters more feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a resource-efficient path toward practical quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a unified overview of protocols and their security.
method: The authors review and classify various quantum cryptographic primitives, discussing their theoretical security guarantees and limitations, and survey current photonic implementations.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives, highlights their security features and constraints, and summarizes experimental progress in photonic platforms.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of protocols beyond QKD, with practical implementations emerging, though many face significant theoretical and experimental challenges.

title: Tight Bounds On Recurrence Time In Closed Quantum Systems
authors: Marcin Kotowski And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Kotowski and Michał Oszmaniec

The evolution of an isolated quantum system inevitably exhibits recurrence: the state returns to the vicinity of its initial condition after finite time. Despite its fundamental nature, a rigorous quantitative understanding of recurrence has been lacking. We establish upper bounds on the recurrence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes tight upper bounds on the recurrence time of closed quantum systems, providing a rigorous quantitative understanding of a fundamental phenomenon.
motivation: Recurrence is a fundamental property of isolated quantum systems, but a rigorous quantitative understanding has been lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap by deriving tight bounds.
method: The authors use mathematical techniques from quantum information and operator theory to analyze the dynamics of closed quantum systems and derive upper bounds on recurrence time.
result: They establish tight upper bounds on the recurrence time, improving upon previous results and providing a more precise characterization.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum recurrence, with implications for fundamental limits on quantum information processing and thermalization.

title: Single-Period Floquet Control Of Bosonic Codes With Quantum Lattice Gates
authors: Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, And Lingzhen Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, and Lingzhen Guo

Bosonic codes constitute a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computing. Existing Floquet protocols enable analytical construction of bosonic codes but typically rely on slow adiabatic ramps with thousands of driving periods. In this Letter, we circumvent this bottleneck by introducing an ana…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060602] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an analytical single-period Floquet protocol for bosonic codes, avoiding slow adiabatic ramps and enabling fast, fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Existing Floquet protocols for bosonic codes require thousands of driving periods, making them slow and impractical. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by designing a single-period protocol.
method: The authors introduce an analytical single-period Floquet protocol using quantum lattice gates, which allows for the construction of bosonic codes without adiabatic ramps.
result: The protocol achieves fast and efficient generation of bosonic codes, significantly reducing the number of driving periods compared to existing methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical advancement in bosonic code construction, potentially accelerating fault-tolerant quantum computing implementations.

title: Quantum Kinetic Uncertainty Relations In Mesoscopic Conductors At Strong Coupling
authors: Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, And Géraldine Haack
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, and Géraldine Haack

Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) set fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport by bounding the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of the dynamical activity, a quantity that counts exchange events between a system and its reservoirs. This framework is well establishe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056302] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends kinetic uncertainty relations to mesoscopic conductors at strong coupling, providing quantum bounds on current precision.
motivation: Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) are fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport, but their validity at strong coupling is unclear. The authors aim to establish quantum KURs for mesoscopic conductors beyond weak coupling.
method: They derive quantum kinetic uncertainty relations for mesoscopic conductors using a full counting statistics approach, incorporating strong system-reservoir coupling and quantum coherence effects.
result: They obtain generalized KURs that bound the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of dynamical activity, with corrections due to strong coupling and quantum coherence.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental precision bounds for quantum transport at strong coupling, advancing the understanding of thermodynamic limits in mesoscopic systems.

title: Experimental Realization Of Thermal Reservoirs With Tunable Temperature In A Trapped-Ion Spin-Boson Simulator
authors: Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, And Guido Pagano
abstract:
Author(s): Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, and Guido Pagano

We propose and demonstrate an experimental scheme to engineer thermal baths with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates for the motional modes of a trapped-ion system. This approach enables robust thermal-state preparation and quantum simulations of open-system dynamics in bosonic …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050604] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a trapped-ion simulator that can engineer thermal reservoirs with independently tunable temperature and dissipation rates for bosonic modes.
motivation: Quantum simulations of open-system dynamics require controllable thermal baths, which are challenging to realize experimentally. The authors aim to provide a flexible platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and dissipative quantum systems.
method: They use a trapped-ion system where the motional modes act as bosonic modes, and they engineer thermal reservoirs by coupling the ions to engineered dissipation, allowing independent control of temperature and dissipation rate.
result: They demonstrate robust thermal-state preparation and show that the engineered baths can simulate open-system dynamics, with tunable parameters verified experimentally.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile tool for quantum simulations of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity, emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but their characterization is challenging. The authors aim to provide a physical interpretation of non-Gaussianity measures.
method: They connect the stellar rank of a quantum state to superselection rules, which restrict operations, and show that this rank corresponds to the minimal number of modes needed to represent the state, linking it to multimode entanglement.
result: The paper demonstrates that stellar rank is physically meaningful, arising from superselection rules, and that it quantifies intrinsic multimode entanglement, offering a new perspective on non-Gaussianity.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum information theory and quantum optics, providing a deeper understanding of non-Gaussianity and its relation to entanglement, which is relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Upper Bounds On The Purity Of Wigner Non-negative Quantum States That Verify The Wigner Entropy Conjecture
authors: Qipeng Qian And Christos N. Gagatsos
abstract:
Author(s): Qipeng Qian and Christos N. Gagatsos

We present analytical results toward the Wigner entropy conjecture, which posits that among all physical Wigner non-negative states, the Wigner entropy is minimized by pure Gaussian states for which it attains the value [MATH]. Working under a minimal set of constraints on the Wigner function, name…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022408] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides analytical upper bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states that satisfy the Wigner entropy conjecture, advancing the understanding of quantum information measures in continuous-variable systems.
motivation: The Wigner entropy conjecture is a fundamental open problem in quantum information, linking Wigner entropy to Gaussian states. Proving or constraining this conjecture is important for characterizing quantum states and their information content.
method: The authors derive analytical upper bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states under minimal constraints on the Wigner function, using techniques from quantum information theory and continuous-variable systems.
result: They obtain explicit upper bounds on purity for states that verify the conjecture, providing new insights into the structure of Wigner non-negative states and their entropy properties.
conclusion: The results contribute to the ongoing effort to prove the Wigner entropy conjecture and deepen our understanding of quantum entropy measures in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Quantum-error-correction-inspired Multiparameter Quantum Metrology
authors: Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, Jonathan A. Gross, And Tyler Volkoff
abstract:
Author(s): Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, Jonathan A. Gross, and Tyler Volkoff

We present a strategy for obtaining optimal probe states and measurement schemes in a class of noiseless multiparameter estimation problems with symmetry among the generators. The key to the framework is the introduction of a set of quantum metrology conditions, analogous to the quantum error correc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for optimal probe states and measurements in multiparameter quantum metrology with symmetry, using quantum error correction conditions.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is important for quantum sensing, but finding optimal strategies is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic method for symmetric problems.
method: They introduce quantum metrology conditions analogous to quantum error correction, and use symmetry to construct optimal probe states and measurement schemes.
result: The framework yields optimal strategies for a class of noiseless multiparameter estimation problems, demonstrated with examples.
conclusion: The work connects quantum error correction and quantum metrology, offering a new tool for designing optimal estimation protocols.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Chaotic Systems With Conservation Laws
authors: Thomas Martin Müller, Silvia Pappalardi, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Martin Müller, Silvia Pappalardi, and Rosario Fazio

Closed chaotic quantum systems relax after a quench from a typical initial state into a Gibbs ensemble. At late times, the relaxation behavior is determined by their conservation laws and hydrodynamics. For specific initial states, this picture can break down. As a result, there exist pairs of initi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080301] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in chaotic systems with conservation laws, showing that certain initial states relax faster than others, and connects this to hydrodynamic modes and symmetries.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in closed chaotic quantum systems is fundamental; the Mpemba effect (where a hotter system cools faster) has quantum analogs that challenge typical thermalization assumptions.
method: The authors analyze chaotic quantum systems with conservation laws, using theoretical frameworks such as hydrodynamics and symmetry-resolved entropies to characterize relaxation times for different initial states.
result: They identify conditions under which the quantum Mpemba effect occurs, linking it to the presence of conservation laws and the initial state's symmetry properties, and demonstrate faster relaxation for certain states.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and relaxation dynamics, with implications for quantum thermalization and information processing.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an elementary derivation of the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators by combining higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relations with a condition on phase-current fluctuations.
motivation: The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and oscillation quality, and a simple derivation is needed to understand its validity and implications.
method: The author combines the higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the bound in one-dimensional systems.
result: The derivation confirms the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators, providing a rigorous foundation for this trade-off.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical basis of the dissipation-coherence bound and offers a simpler proof that may facilitate further applications in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Conservative Dissipation Shapes Symmetry Breaking In Nonequilibrium Currents
authors: Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, and Daniel Maria Busiello

Most natural thermodynamic systems operate far from equilibrium, developing persistent currents and organizing into nonequilibrium stationary states (NESSs). Yet, the general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033126] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how conservative dissipation in nonequilibrium systems shapes symmetry breaking and persistent currents, providing a general framework for understanding nonequilibrium stationary states.
motivation: Most natural systems operate far from equilibrium, yet general principles governing how driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain unclear. The authors aim to uncover these principles.
method: They develop a theoretical framework analyzing the role of conservative dissipation in nonequilibrium currents, likely using stochastic thermodynamics and symmetry arguments.
result: The paper reveals how conservative dissipation influences symmetry breaking in nonequilibrium currents, leading to novel insights into the organization of nonequilibrium stationary states.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics and provide a general principle for symmetry breaking in driven systems.

title: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Gates Using Polynomial Phase Gates And On-demand Noise Biasing
authors: Minh T. P. Nguyen And Mackenzie H. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T. P. Nguyen and Mackenzie H. Shaw

The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error correcting code uses a bosonic mode to encode a logical qubit and has the attractive property that its logical Clifford gates can be implemented using Gaussian unitary gates. In contrast, a direct unitary implementation of the [MATH] gate using the cubic phase …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033107] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford GKP gates using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing, advancing quantum error correction.
motivation: Direct unitary implementation of non-Clifford gates like the cubic phase gate in GKP codes is challenging; the authors aim to provide a more practical fault-tolerant approach.
method: They combine polynomial phase gates with on-demand noise biasing to implement non-Clifford gates, analyzing the resulting error correction properties.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with improved noise resilience compared to direct implementations.
conclusion: The work offers a viable path for universal quantum computation with GKP codes, enhancing the practicality of bosonic error correction.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to convert common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome the challenge of generating and stabilizing multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum sensing and simulation, by exploiting dissipation rather than avoiding it.
method: They propose a scheme using a common cavity to mediate dissipative interactions among many spin ensembles, engineering the dissipation to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability via external controls.
result: The approach yields robust steady-state entanglement that can be tailored for ultraprecise sensing and for realizing topological many-body states, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical pathway for using engineered dissipation in hybrid quantum systems to create and stabilize complex entangled states, with potential applications in quantum metrology and many-body physics.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: To provide a practical, integrated solution for certified quantum randomness generation that does not require full device characterization, addressing the need for compact and reliable QRNGs.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip implementing a contextuality-based protocol for semi-device-independent randomness generation, and experimentally characterize its performance.
result: The on-chip device successfully generates random numbers with certified randomness, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated semi-device-independent QRNGs.
conclusion: The work provides a significant step towards practical, chip-scale quantum randomness generation with security guarantees, relevant to quantum cryptography and information processing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To understand and mitigate loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, which are crucial for hybrid quantum systems and quantum information processing.
method: The authors experimentally characterize and optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators, likely using fabrication and measurement techniques to assess phonon coherence and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity, and identify materials-related loss mechanisms, leading to a blueprint for future quantum acoustics devices.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by enhancing the performance of mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, with implications for quantum transduction and memory.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, targeting distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires high-fidelity entanglement between distant nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and require costly distillation. The goal is to reduce the resource overhead for logical Bell pair preparation.
method: The protocol uses quantum error correction and entanglement distillation techniques, optimized for low spacetime volume and 2D local connectivity, to prepare logical Bell pairs from noisy physical ones.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pairs with significantly reduced spacetime cost compared to existing methods, and requires only 2D local device connectivity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for generating logical Bell pairs, which is a key resource for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum networks.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during dispersive readout limit transmon qubit fidelity, and a nonlinear coupling may mitigate these errors.
method: The authors perform experiments on a transmon with cosφ coupling and compare with numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the nonlinear coupling.
result: They demonstrate suppression of measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The nonlinear cosφ coupling is a promising approach for improving transmon readout, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states required to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank dictates the minimum number of Gaussian states needed for state preparation, the compression cost, and the number of measurements required for tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and practical quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, revealing where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum information processing, as these functions underpin many quantum algorithms and protocols.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum computational complexity theory and possibly query complexity or oracle models.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, identifying regimes where quantum algorithms may outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theoretical foundations of quantum computing, potentially guiding the development of quantum algorithms for matrix-related tasks.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and introducing logical measurement statistics for stability analysis.
motivation: Understanding the stability and decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes, focusing on the role of measurement outcomes in decoding and introducing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They demonstrate that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they provide new criteria for stability based on logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and have implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: The search for new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing and networking.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to study a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring its spin coherence and optical properties.
result: They find a defect with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering a combination of properties competitive with existing spin qubit systems.

title: Hybrid Light-matter Excitations And Spontaneous Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking In Two-dimensional Josephson Junctions
authors: V. Varrica, G. Falci, E. Paladino, And F. M. D. Pellegrino
abstract:
Author(s): V. Varrica, G. Falci, E. Paladino, and F. M. D. Pellegrino

Here, the authors show that inductive coupling between a superconducting resonator and a short, wide two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction induces a phase transition in the global light–matter ground state. The resulting phase, which spontaneously breaks time-reversal symmetry, carries a finite equilibrium supercurrent at phase difference =π, where an isolated conventional Josephson junction carries no equilibrium supercurrent. The hybrid light–matter excitation spectrum provides spectroscopic fingerprints of the transition, while highly transparent transport channels determine the critical coupling.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that inductive coupling between a superconducting resonator and a two-dimensional Josephson junction induces a phase transition with spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking, leading to a finite supercurrent at phase difference π.
motivation: To explore hybrid light-matter systems in Josephson junctions, which are relevant for quantum information processing and fundamental physics.
method: The authors model a short, wide two-dimensional Josephson junction inductively coupled to a superconducting resonator, analyzing the ground state and excitation spectrum.
result: They find a phase transition in the global light-matter ground state that breaks time-reversal symmetry, resulting in a finite equilibrium supercurrent at phase difference π, with the critical coupling determined by highly transparent transport channels.
conclusion: The hybrid light-matter excitation spectrum provides spectroscopic fingerprints of the transition, offering a new platform for studying quantum phase transitions and potential applications in quantum devices.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
