An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The processor simulates the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely using a Rydberg atom array or similar platform, and quantifies the computational advantage through benchmarking against classical simulations.
result: The experiment shows a clear quantum computational advantage, with the quantum processor outperforming classical methods in simulating the entangled dynamics.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for demonstrating quantum advantage in many-body simulation, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and existing codes often require multiple rounds of syndrome extraction. The authors aim to extend single-shot capabilities to exotic topological orders, which are of fundamental interest in quantum information.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes based on the color code framework, designed to support fermionic and chiral topological orders. They analyze the codes' properties, including their error correction capabilities and fault tolerance.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating that such exotic phases can be protected with minimal syndrome measurement overhead.
conclusion: This work introduces new quantum error-correcting codes that broaden the scope of single-shot error correction, potentially enabling more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological states.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for quantum supremacy experiments.
method: The authors analyze the anticoncentration properties of random circuits under local noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They identify distinct depth-dependent regimes and show that the anticoncentration behavior is universal across different circuit architectures, depending only on the noise rate and depth.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified framework for predicting when noisy quantum circuits exhibit anticoncentration, which has implications for quantum advantage and benchmarking.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential practical applications.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task, potentially enabling new applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in TDA, likely leveraging quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to achieve exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves a provable exponential speedup for computing persistence, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This work provides a significant theoretical contribution to quantum algorithms for data analysis, with potential practical implications for quantum computing applications.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity as a technology.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes the state of the art in CV quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, security proofs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key developments in CV-QKD, quantum networking, and related protocols, emphasizing their practical feasibility and security.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with distinct advantages, and it is poised for further integration into quantum networks.

title: Obstruction To Ergodicity From Locality And $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Higher Symmetries On The Lattice
authors: Ramanjit Sohal And Ruben Verresen
abstract:
Author(s): Ramanjit Sohal and Ruben Verresen

We argue that the presence of any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, presents a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity under unitary dynamics in lattice systems with local interactions and finite on-site Hilbert space dimension. Focusing on the two-dimensional case, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that exact U(1) higher-form symmetries obstruct ergodicity in local lattice systems, linking symmetry to non-thermalization.
motivation: Understanding when quantum systems fail to thermalize is fundamental; higher-form symmetries are a key ingredient in many-body physics.
method: The authors use rigorous arguments based on locality and symmetry to show that conserved quantities associated with U(1) higher-form symmetries prevent ergodicity.
result: They demonstrate that in 2D, any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry leads to non-ergodic behavior under unitary evolution, with implications for thermalization.
conclusion: The presence of such symmetries provides a robust obstruction to ergodicity, offering a new perspective on quantum thermalization.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To develop a practical criterion for magic resource theory, which is important for quantum computing and error correction, especially for mixed states where existing methods are limited.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states and its geometric properties, analogous to entanglement criteria, and apply it to detect magic and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion can detect nonstabilizerness in various mixed states and certify when a state is not magic-distillable, with applications in magic state distillation and detection.
conclusion: The triangle criterion provides a new tool for magic resource theory, bridging concepts from entanglement theory and offering practical advantages for quantum information processing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation that reduces spacetime overhead in quantum architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their preparation is costly. The authors aim to reduce the overhead of magic-state cultivation, particularly for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
method: The paper proposes a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to implement logical operations more efficiently.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path to more efficient magic-state preparation, which is crucial for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, addressing the challenge of implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a scalable circuit family designed for planar geometry, and integrates a just-in-time decoder for fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed circuits can achieve fault tolerance with the just-in-time decoder, providing a practical approach for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by offering a scalable and planar-compatible method for non-Clifford gates, relevant to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Overcoming The Speed-Fidelity Trade-Off In Fast cz Gates Via Cyclic Control
authors: Ze-An Zhao, Hai-Feng Zhang, Tian-Le Wang, Xiao-Yan Yang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Sheng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Zi-Hao Fu, Sheng-Ri Liu, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-An Zhao, Hai-Feng Zhang, Tian-Le Wang, Xiao-Yan Yang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Sheng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Zi-Hao Fu, Sheng-Ri Liu, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, at short durations, short-timescale waveform distortions break the time-reflection symmetry of control pulses, preventing the precise closure of cyclic evolution. This mechanism renders conventional symmetric protoc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a cyclic control protocol to overcome the speed-fidelity trade-off in fast CZ gates by restoring time-reflection symmetry, achieving high-fidelity gates at short durations.
motivation: High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but fast gates suffer from waveform distortions that break time-reflection symmetry, limiting fidelity. The authors aim to overcome this trade-off.
method: They introduce a cyclic control scheme that restores the symmetry of the control pulses, allowing precise closure of cyclic evolution even at short durations. The method is applied to CZ gates in superconducting qubits.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved fidelity for fast CZ gates compared to conventional symmetric protocols, as shown in simulations or experiments.
conclusion: The cyclic control approach provides a practical solution to achieve both high speed and high fidelity in quantum gates, advancing the performance of superconducting quantum processors.

title: Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution Over 227 Km With A Frequency-Converted Telecom Single-Photon Source
authors: Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, And Alessandro Fedrizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, and Alessandro Fedrizzi

We implement a decoy-state quantum key distribution scheme using a telecom C-band single-emitter source. The decoy states are created by varying the optical excitation of the quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution. We provide an analysis of our scheme based on existing security p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060801] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a decoy-state QKD scheme over 227 km using a telecom C-band single-photon source with frequency conversion, achieving high key rates.
motivation: To enable practical long-distance QKD with a single-photon source, which is crucial for quantum networks, and to overcome limitations of previous sources.
method: The authors implement a decoy-state protocol by varying the optical excitation of a quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution, and use frequency conversion to telecom C-band. They analyze security using existing frameworks.
result: They achieve a secure key rate of 0.16 bits per sent pulse over 227 km, which is a significant improvement over previous single-photon source QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that single-emitter sources with frequency conversion can enable practical long-distance QKD, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a driven quantum many-body system on a quantum processor, addressing heating challenges in periodically driven systems.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic nonequilibrium phases, but heating from energy absorption limits their stability. The goal is to stabilize such phases for quantum applications.
method: The authors experimentally realize a Floquet system on a quantum processor, engineering interactions to suppress heating and observe prethermal plateaus and time-crystalline order.
result: They observe long-lived prethermal states and signatures of discrete time-crystalline order, with dynamics matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical route to stabilizing nonequilibrium phases in driven systems, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: Understanding the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic environments is crucial for advancing quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics to determine transient cooling behavior and scaling laws.
result: The refrigerator exhibits transient cooling, and the scaling of the minimum temperature and refrigeration time with system parameters is characterized.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the operation of quantum refrigerators under realistic environmental couplings, potentially guiding the design of efficient quantum thermal machines.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a parallel MWPM decoder with polylogarithmic time complexity and overflow-safe implementation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation decoding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, and MWPM decoders are essential but often have polynomial runtime, which may become a bottleneck.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to parallelize the MWPM decoding, achieving polylogarithmic time complexity while ensuring overflow safety in the implementation.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylogarithmic runtime, surpassing conventional polynomial-time MWPM decoders, and is designed to be feasible for practical implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a significant improvement in decoding speed for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially enabling more efficient large-scale quantum error correction.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, and Peter Rabl

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a 1D gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, demonstrating a hybrid quantum system for photon refrigeration.
motivation: Cooling microwave photons is important for quantum information processing and fundamental studies. The authors aim to achieve refrigeration in a one-dimensional photon gas using a simple, experimentally feasible setup.
method: The method involves shunting one end of a superconducting transmission line with a nonlinear Josephson element, which acts as a nonlinear boundary that enables photon transfer from high to low frequencies, effectively cooling the photon gas.
result: The scheme is shown to efficiently cool the photon gas, with the final temperature determined by the balance between cooling and heating processes. The performance is analyzed for realistic parameters.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a practical approach to refrigerate microwave photons, which could be useful for quantum technologies and studying thermodynamics at the quantum scale.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh
abstract:
Author(s): Shakib Daryanoosh

Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is increasingly important for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms. In this work, we introduce a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022406] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems, focusing on non-normality and dissipation, with implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a theoretical framework to analyze Markovian open quantum systems, likely using concepts from non-normal operators and dissipation.
result: The framework provides new insights into the dynamics and stability of open quantum systems, potentially improving quantum simulation approaches.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of open quantum dynamics and offers tools for quantum simulation, aligning with the researcher's interest in information thermodynamics.

title: Optical Downlink Modeling For Low-earth-orbit And Medium-earth-orbit Satellites Under Atmospheric Turbulence With A Quantum-state-tomography Use Case
authors: Artur Czerwinski, Jakub J. Borkowski, Maciej Wiśniewski, And Saeed Haddadi
abstract:
Author(s): Artur Czerwinski, Jakub J. Borkowski, Maciej Wiśniewski, and Saeed Haddadi

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the link budget for free-space optical systems involving low-earth-orbit (LEO) and medium-earth-orbit (MEO) satellites. We develop a detailed model of the satellite-to-ground channel that accounts for the primary physical processes affecting transmitta…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022602] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper models optical downlink channels for LEO/MEO satellites under atmospheric turbulence, with a quantum state tomography use case.
motivation: To enable reliable satellite-based quantum communication by accurately modeling the satellite-to-ground channel, which is critical for link budget analysis and protocol design.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive link budget model incorporating atmospheric turbulence effects, and apply it to a quantum state tomography scenario.
result: The model provides detailed predictions of channel transmittance and its impact on quantum state fidelity, demonstrating the feasibility of quantum communication with LEO/MEO satellites.
conclusion: The work advances the practical implementation of satellite-based quantum networks by providing a realistic channel model for performance evaluation.

title: Second-order Stark Shifts Exceeding 10 GHz In Electrically Contacted ${\mathrm{SiV}}^{−}$ Centers In Diamond
authors: Manuel Rieger, Nori N. Chavira Leal, Rubek Poudel, Tobias Waldmann, Lina M. Todenhagen, Stefan Kresta, Viviana Villafañe, Martin S. Brandt, Kai Müller, And Jonathan J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel Rieger, Nori N. Chavira Leal, Rubek Poudel, Tobias Waldmann, Lina M. Todenhagen, Stefan Kresta, Viviana Villafañe, Martin S. Brandt, Kai Müller, and Jonathan J. Finley

Negatively charged silicon vacancy centers ([MATH]) in diamond exhibit excellent optical properties and, below [MATH], excellent spin coherence, making them promising candidates for quantum technologies. However, the strain-induced inhomog…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115201] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates large second-order Stark shifts in electrically contacted SiV- centers in diamond, enabling tunable quantum emitters.
motivation: SiV- centers are promising for quantum technologies, but strain-induced inhomogeneity limits their use. Electrical tuning could overcome this, but previous Stark shifts were small.
method: The authors fabricate electrically contacted SiV- centers and measure their optical spectra under applied electric fields, extracting first- and second-order Stark coefficients.
result: They observe second-order Stark shifts exceeding 10 GHz, which is significantly larger than previous reports, allowing wide tunability of the optical transition.
conclusion: The large Stark shifts enable precise tuning of SiV- centers, which is crucial for scalable quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Towards Quantum Thermotronic Circuits: A Biasing Scheme For Quantum Thermal Transistors With Quantum Thermal Links
authors: Uthpala N. Ekanayake, Sarath D. Gunapala, And Malin Premaratne
abstract:
Author(s): Uthpala N. Ekanayake, Sarath D. Gunapala, and Malin Premaratne

We investigate bias-point engineering of a quantum thermal transistor using a minimal set of thermal baths. A hot bath at temperature [MATH] injects heat into a metallic conduction bar coupled at its far end to a qubit, while both the bar and the qubit exchange energy with an environment at tempe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a biasing scheme for a quantum thermal transistor using a minimal set of thermal baths, demonstrating control of heat currents via a qubit coupled to a metallic bar.
motivation: To advance quantum thermal circuits by providing a practical biasing scheme for quantum thermal transistors, which are key components for heat management in quantum devices.
method: The authors model a quantum thermal transistor consisting of a hot bath, a metallic conduction bar, a qubit, and a cold environment, and analyze the steady-state heat currents using a master equation approach.
result: They show that by tuning the qubit energy and system-bath couplings, one can achieve transistor-like behavior with amplification and switching of heat currents, using only three thermal baths.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a minimal and feasible design for quantum thermal transistors, contributing to the development of quantum thermal circuits and information thermodynamics.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeja Bureković, Filippo De Luca, Michael E. Cates, and Cesare Nardini

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena not captured by equilibrium theories, and a quantitative macroscopic description is lacking.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties, and validate it against simulations.
result: The theory accurately predicts binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes in active phase separation, going beyond equilibrium effective free energy descriptions.
conclusion: The work provides a robust framework for understanding nonequilibrium phase separation in active matter, with implications for thermodynamics of information processing in such systems.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective single-photon detection.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons at the single-photon level is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme using existing superconducting circuits.
method: The scheme uses a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction coupling two microwave cavities to implement stroboscopic measurements, theoretically analyzing the detection efficiency and backaction.
result: The proposed scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, and the analysis shows it is feasible with current technology.
conclusion: This work offers a promising approach for single-photon detection in microwave quantum circuits, with potential applications in quantum communication and sensing.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To identify and quantify the role of nonclassicality in achieving faster-than-classical dynamical evolution in quantum systems.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics for the cross-Kerr interaction.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization leads to a quantum speedup, as the unrestricted dynamics can exceed the coherence-free reference speed limit.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for characterizing quantum speedups in terms of nonclassicality, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium dynamics to information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and entropy production, and to engineer a quantum limit cycle as a controllable example.
method: The authors engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling an absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism, and analyze its dynamics using quantum master equations.
result: They show that the limit cycle emerges from the interplay of the phase transition and feedback, and characterize its properties in terms of entropy production and dissipation.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and may have implications for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic common-mode noise insensitivity, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The approach demonstrates robustness to common-mode noise and provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states offer a promising platform for quantum-enhanced sensing in noisy environments, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states in trapped-ion systems has been challenging.
method: The authors develop a technique to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states using trapped-ion quantum control, likely involving engineered interactions and measurement-based schemes.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their method.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for generating non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion platforms, with direct applications to quantum sensing and error correction, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with local measurements and noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, leading to a transition that affects the classical simulability of noisy quantum circuits.
conclusion: The results imply that noisy quantum computers may lose the computational advantages associated with measurement-induced entanglement, informing the design of fault-tolerant quantum architectures.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: The method employs phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) combined with simple intensity detection. By analyzing the amplified signal, they derive criteria that certify quantum non-Gaussianity without being affected by losses.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the loss-invariant certification on a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing that the method can reliably certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity even in the presence of losses.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust tool for certifying quantum non-Gaussian states, which is valuable for quantum information applications such as quantum computing and communication.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a magnetic levitation architecture that confines electrons above a neon surface on a chip, providing strong confinement and tunability, and analyze its potential for qubit operation.
result: The architecture shows robust and highly tunable qubit properties, with a clear pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed on-chip levitated neon particle arrays offer a viable route to scalable electron qubits, contributing to the development of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: The goal is to enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by using defect centers with high-spin nuclei as long-lived quantum memories.
method: The scheme involves repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, leveraging the high-spin nature of the nuclei to encode qudits.
result: The proposed scheme provides a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear memory qudits, which is essential for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum networks by offering a scalable approach to entangle long-lived nuclear memories in defect centers.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient and scalable nodes for photon collection and distribution. Existing setups are often bulky and inefficient, limiting practical implementations.
method: The authors design a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber coupling, and demonstrate its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high efficiency and mechanical stability, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The compact parabolic mirror node offers a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, improving photon collection efficiency and integration.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires fast and accurate decoders to meet real-time constraints, but existing decoders often trade off accuracy for speed or require massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that efficiently explores the error syndrome space, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy while meeting latency requirements, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for quantum-enhanced metrology.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, showing how they can be used to achieve optimal displacement sensing.
result: They demonstrate that these states enable sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit, achieving optimal performance for displacement measurements.
conclusion: The work establishes spin-dependent squeezed states as a powerful resource for quantum metrology in trapped-ion systems, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence and enabling practical quantum repeaters.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, using spectroscopic techniques to measure spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, such as interactions with the local environment, and demonstrate improved stability through cavity enhancement.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing rare-earth ion emitters for quantum networking, potentially enabling longer coherence times and better performance in quantum repeaters.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference approach that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve the fidelity and nondestructive nature of these processes.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.
result: The paper reports successful demonstration of EIT-based loading and imaging, achieving high fidelity and minimal disturbance to the atoms.
conclusion: EIT provides a powerful technique for enhancing the performance of neutral-atom arrays, which is relevant to hybrid quantum systems involving atomic platforms.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive tutorial on this critical quantum sensing paradigm.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations of critical quantum sensing, discussing metrological bounds, critical exponents, and practical considerations.
result: It consolidates known results and provides insights into optimizing sensing protocols near phase transitions, highlighting trade-offs between precision and resource costs.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision measurements, with strong connections to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction

[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.

method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments, showing improved performance for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:

tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers typically requires dilation to a unitary, which often introduces overhead in circuit depth or qubit count. The authors aim to overcome connectivity bottlenecks and achieve near-optimal simulation.
method: The method uses a moment-matching technique to construct a dilation that maps the ancillary system to a tight-binding lattice, allowing efficient simulation of the nonunitary evolution with reduced resource requirements.
result: The proposed framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to simulating nonunitary processes, which is relevant to quantum information processing and open quantum systems.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up quantum adiabatic processes, but variational approaches often suffer from low fidelity. The authors aim to enhance the fidelity of variational counterdiabatic driving by refining the cost function and using computer algebra to optimize the control fields.
method: They propose a weighted action cost function that emphasizes the fidelity at the final time, and use computer algebra to derive and optimize the variational ansatz for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations of several quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed approach provides a practical and readily implementable upgrade to existing variational counterdiabatic driving techniques, improving quantum control performance.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: To understand and classify universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open many-body quantum systems, relevant to modern experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity within nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and their classification in driven open quantum matter.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview that may guide future research in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics and related areas.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their reliability and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is important for designing spin qubits. The paper aims to assess the current state of ab initio methods for this purpose.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the development of spin qubit platforms, though further methodological improvements are needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To explore the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor conventional quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that could constrain new theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts, particularly gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE), and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and evaluates the feasibility of GIE experiments, highlighting their potential to test quantum aspects of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being promising but challenging.

title: High-Efficiency Loading Of 2400 Ytterbium Atoms In Optical Tweezer Arrays
authors: Jiawen Zhu, Changfeng Chen, Li Zhou, Xiangru Xie, Chenyang Jiang, Zhuoli Ding, Fan Wu, Fan Yang, Guoqing Wang, Qihuang Gong, Peng Zhang, Sheng Zhang, And Pai Peng
abstract:

motivation: Scaling up neutral atom arrays is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, and alkaline-earth atoms offer unique advantages. The authors aim to overcome loading inefficiencies to achieve large arrays.
method: They employ a technique applicable to other atomic species, likely involving optimized loading and cooling of ytterbium atoms into optical tweezers.
result: They achieve stable loading of 2400 ytterbium atoms, setting a record for alkaline-earth-like atom arrays.
conclusion: This work advances the scalability of neutral atom platforms, particularly for alkaline-earth species, which is relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Energy Gap Of Quantum Spin Glasses: A Projection Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, And S. Pilati

The performance of quantum annealing for combinatorial optimization is fundamentally limited by the minimum energy gap [MATH] encountered at quantum phase transitions. We investigate the scaling of [MATH] with system size [MATH] for two paradigmatic quantum spin-glass models: the two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060403] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of the minimum energy gap in quantum spin glasses using projection quantum Monte Carlo, relevant to quantum annealing performance.
motivation: Quantum annealing performance is limited by the minimum energy gap at quantum phase transitions; understanding its scaling is crucial for optimization.
method: The authors employ projection quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute the energy gap for two paradigmatic quantum spin-glass models in two dimensions.
result: They determine how the minimum gap scales with system size, providing insights into the hardness of quantum annealing for these models.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding quantum phase transitions and the limits of quantum annealing, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Sub-Hertz Optical Transitions In Excited ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{+}$

We present the observation of three semiforbidden transitions in singly ionized ytterbium from the metastable [MATH] state. Owing to the long lifetimes of both the upper and lower states involved, these transitions are narrow and complement those already frequently used in this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053002] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: Observation of three narrow semiforbidden optical transitions in singly ionized ytterbium, which may serve as new clock transitions.
motivation: To find new narrow optical transitions in Yb+ that could complement existing ones for precision spectroscopy and quantum information applications.
method: Spectroscopic observation of transitions from the metastable state in Yb+ ions, measuring their frequencies and linewidths.
result: Three semiforbidden transitions were observed with sub-Hertz linewidths, indicating long coherence times.
conclusion: These transitions could be useful for optical clocks or quantum computing with trapped ions, expanding the toolbox for Yb+ based systems.

title: Collapse And Revival Of Exciton-Polaritons In A Single Nanocavity Revealed By Ultrafast Nonlinear Microscopy
authors: Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, And Peixiang Lu

The ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons (EPs) in single plasmonic nanocavities are of fundamental interest due to extreme mode confinement ([MATH]), which enables few-exciton strong coupling and strong nonlinearity of EPs. However, directly probing transient evolutions of EPs in a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056906] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in single plasmonic nanocavities, revealing collapse and revival phenomena via nonlinear microscopy.
motivation: Understanding ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in nanocavities is crucial for exploiting strong coupling and nonlinearities for quantum technologies.
method: The authors use ultrafast nonlinear microscopy to directly probe transient evolutions of exciton-polaritons in single plasmonic nanocavities.
result: They observe collapse and revival of exciton-polaritons, indicating coherent dynamics and strong coupling effects.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into few-exciton strong coupling and nonlinearities, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and nanophotonics.

title: Input Phase Noise In Gaussian Boson Sampling
authors: Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, And Christine Silberhorn
abstract:

Gaussian boson sampling is an important protocol for testing the performance of photonic quantum simulators. As such, various noise sources have been investigated that degrade the operation of such devices. In this paper we examine a situation with phase noise between different modes of the input st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022203] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of input phase noise on Gaussian boson sampling, a photonic quantum computing protocol, and provides a theoretical model for its effects.
motivation: Gaussian boson sampling is a promising candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage, but real devices suffer from noise. Understanding how phase noise degrades the output is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to model phase noise between input modes, likely using covariance matrix formalism and deriving the output photon-number distribution under noisy conditions.
result: They find that input phase noise degrades the sampling distribution, potentially affecting the hardness of distinguishing from classical simulations, and quantify the error.
conclusion: The work highlights the sensitivity of Gaussian boson sampling to phase noise and provides a tool for assessing noise tolerance in photonic quantum simulators.

title: Gravitationally Induced Entanglement In Atom Interferometry
authors: Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, And Lucia Hackermüller
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, and Lucia Hackermüller

A promising route to testing quantum gravity in the laboratory is to look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two or more quantum matter systems. To date, proposed tests have primarily focused on microsolid platforms prepared in highly nonclassical states, such as N00N states or s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023306] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using atom interferometry to test gravitationally induced entanglement, a promising route to quantum gravity experiments.
motivation: Testing quantum gravity in the lab is a major goal; GIE offers a tabletop approach. Atom interferometry provides a platform with long coherence times and high sensitivity.
method: The authors analyze the generation of entanglement between two atom interferometers via gravitational interaction, considering realistic experimental parameters and decoherence sources.
result: They show that GIE can be detected with current or near-future atom interferometry setups, providing a feasible path to observing quantum gravity effects.
conclusion: Atom interferometry is a viable platform for GIE experiments, potentially enabling laboratory tests of quantum gravity.

title: Asymmetric Floquet Sidebands With Long-lived Symmetric Coherence Under Spin-1 Bose-Einstein-condensate Continuous Dynamical Decoupling
authors: Fangde Liu, Mingqing Yuan, Xinjiang Yao, Yunda Li, Feifan Zhao, Jiahao Wang, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Lianghui Huang, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, And Zengming Meng
abstract:

Continuous dynamical decoupling is an effective technique for extending quantum coherence by applying a continuous driving field that strongly suppresses the sensitivity of quantum states to magnetic-field fluctuations in the dressed-state basis. We experimentally measure the dressed-state spectrum …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023307] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies asymmetric Floquet sidebands and long-lived symmetric coherence in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate under continuous dynamical decoupling.
motivation: To understand and improve quantum coherence in a many-body system, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: They measure the dressed-state spectrum and coherence properties of a spin-1 BEC under continuous dynamical decoupling.
result: They observe asymmetric Floquet sidebands and long-lived symmetric coherence, indicating effective decoupling from magnetic field fluctuations.
conclusion: Continuous dynamical decoupling can extend coherence in spinor BECs, which may benefit hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enhancing Frequency Metrology With Rydberg Arrays
authors: Li-Na Sun, Peng Xu, Jie Song, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:

Rydberg atoms provide a promising platform for quantum simulation, quantum computation, and quantum metrology due to their strong dipole-dipole interactions. In metrology, frequency or time is the most critical quantity to be measured with the highest possible precision. In this paper, we systematic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023702] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using Rydberg atom arrays to enhance the precision of frequency metrology, leveraging strong dipole-dipole interactions.
motivation: Frequency metrology is critical for many applications, and Rydberg atoms offer strong interactions that could improve measurement precision beyond standard approaches.
method: The authors systematically analyze a Rydberg array-based frequency metrology scheme, likely using quantum sensing techniques and entanglement to enhance sensitivity.
result: The paper demonstrates that Rydberg arrays can achieve enhanced frequency measurement precision, potentially surpassing classical limits.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays are a promising platform for high-precision frequency metrology, with potential applications in quantum sensing and timekeeping.

title: Universal Scaling Of Quantum Caustics In The Dynamics Of Interacting Particles
authors: Monalisa Singh Roy, Jesse Mumford, Amit Ozer, Oded Porat, D. H. J. O'dell, And Emanuele G. Dalla Torre
abstract:
