Recent theoretical studies have predicted the existence of caustics in many-body quantum dynamics, where they manifest as extended regions of enhanced probability density that obey temporal and spatial scaling relations. Focusing on the transverse-field Ising model, we investigate the dynamics initi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal scaling of quantum caustics in the transverse-field Ising model, connecting many-body quantum dynamics to thermodynamic-like scaling behavior.
motivation: To understand universal features of many-body quantum dynamics, specifically caustics that appear as enhanced probability density regions with scaling relations.
method: The authors investigate the dynamics of the transverse-field Ising model, focusing on the formation and scaling of quantum caustics, likely using analytical and numerical approaches.
result: They find universal temporal and spatial scaling relations for quantum caustics in interacting particle systems.
conclusion: The work reveals universal scaling behavior in many-body quantum dynamics, which may have implications for understanding non-equilibrium quantum systems.

title: Quantum Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland And Generalized Constraints In Iterative Quantum Algorithms
authors: Lucas T. Brady And Stuart Hadfield
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas T. Brady and Stuart Hadfield

Too often, quantum computer scientists seek to create new algorithms entirely fresh from new cloth when there are extensive and optimized classical algorithms that can be generalized wholesale. At the same time, one may seek to maintain classical advantages of performance and runtime bounds, while e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022404] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical DPLL and constraint satisfaction algorithms to the quantum setting, aiming to leverage classical algorithmic advantages in iterative quantum algorithms.
motivation: The authors argue that quantum algorithm design often overlooks the extensive body of optimized classical algorithms, and propose to adapt classical DPLL and generalized constraints to quantum computing to maintain performance and runtime advantages.
method: They develop quantum versions of DPLL and generalized constraint satisfaction, integrating them into iterative quantum algorithms, likely using amplitude amplification or other quantum subroutines.
result: The paper presents a framework for quantum DPLL and generalized constraints, potentially offering speedups or improved scalability for certain problem classes, though specific numerical results are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising direction for hybrid classical-quantum algorithm design, but its impact on core quantum information theory is moderate, as it focuses on algorithmic techniques rather than fundamental information-theoretic results.

title: Floquet-informed Learning Of Time-periodic Hamiltonians
authors: Keren Li
abstract:
Author(s): Keren Li

Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is important for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, yet generic time-domain reconstruction methods, when applied directly, can require dense temporal sampling and overparametrized time-slice descriptions. Informed by the Floquet theorem, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022405] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-informed learning method to efficiently reconstruct time-periodic Hamiltonians from limited measurements.
motivation: Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is crucial for validating and controlling driven quantum systems, but generic time-domain methods require dense sampling and overparametrized descriptions.
method: The method leverages the Floquet theorem to reduce the parameter space, enabling efficient Hamiltonian learning from sparse time-domain data.
result: The approach demonstrates accurate reconstruction with reduced sampling requirements compared to generic methods.
conclusion: Floquet-informed learning provides a practical and efficient tool for Hamiltonian characterization in driven quantum platforms.

title: Learning Spectral Density Functions In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Felipe Peleteiro, João Victor Shiguetsugo Kawanami Lima, Pedro Marcelo Prado, Felipe Fernandes Fanchini, And Ariel Norambuena
abstract:
Author(s): Felipe Peleteiro, João Victor Shiguetsugo Kawanami Lima, Pedro Marcelo Prado, Felipe Fernandes Fanchini, and Ariel Norambuena

Spectral density functions quantify how environmental modes couple to quantum systems and govern their open dynamics. Inferring such frequency-dependent functions from time-domain measurements is an ill-conditioned inverse problem. Here, we use exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to infer spectral density functions of open quantum systems from time-domain measurements, addressing an ill-conditioned inverse problem.
motivation: Spectral density functions are crucial for understanding open quantum system dynamics, but inferring them from measurements is challenging due to ill-conditioning.
method: The authors employ exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing and use machine learning techniques to reconstruct the spectral density from simulated time-domain data.
result: The method successfully recovers spectral densities for various models, demonstrating robustness and accuracy even with limited data.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for characterizing environmental couplings, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Continuous Accumulation Of Cold Atoms In An Optical Cavity
authors: Edward Gheorghita, Sebastian Wald, Andrea Pupić, And Onur Hosten
abstract:
Author(s): Edward Gheorghita, Sebastian Wald, Andrea Pupić, and Onur Hosten

Continuously operating atom-light interfaces represent a key prerequisite for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors. Here, we demonstrate continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in a shallow intracavity dipole trap, realizing this regime. The key ingredient is a l…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in an optical cavity, enabling steady-state atom-light interfaces for quantum sensors and processors.
motivation: Continuous operation of atom-light interfaces is crucial for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors, but achieving continuous accumulation of cold atoms in a cavity has been challenging.
method: The authors use a shallow intracavity dipole trap to continuously accumulate sub-Doppler-cooled atoms, leveraging the cavity's optical potential to confine atoms while maintaining cooling.
result: They demonstrate continuous accumulation of cold atoms in the cavity, achieving a steady-state atomic ensemble suitable for atom-light interfacing.
conclusion: This work establishes a practical approach for continuous atom-light interfaces, advancing hybrid quantum systems for sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Preparation Of A Quasi-two-dimensional Bose Mixture Of Ultracold $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ And $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ Atoms
authors: Ji-Kai Liao, Hao-Ran Zhang, Xiao-Rong Yu, Ya-Qun Qi, Yi-Cheng Guo, Bo Zhao, Jun Rui, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

Quantum gases confined in reduced dimensions have enabled the observation of many exotic quantum phenomena. While existing experiments primarily focus on homonuclear systems, we report here on the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023303] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold sodium and rubidium atoms, a key step for studying quantum phenomena in reduced dimensions.
motivation: To extend quantum gas experiments to heteronuclear systems in reduced dimensions, enabling the study of novel quantum phenomena and interactions not accessible in homonuclear systems.
method: The authors use a combination of laser cooling, magnetic trapping, and evaporative cooling to create a quantum degenerate mixture of 23Na and 87Rb, and then confine it to a quasi-two-dimensional geometry using an optical lattice or similar potential.
result: They achieve efficient preparation of the quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear Bose mixture, demonstrating quantum degeneracy and stable confinement.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for exploring quantum physics with heteronuclear mixtures in low dimensions, with potential applications in quantum simulation and precision measurements.

title: Long-time Entanglement In Open Atomic Systems Driven By A Dissipative Squeezed Cavity
authors: Hao Liu, Mingzhu Weng, And Tian Tian

Squeezing has attracted increasing attention as a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity field. Going beyond the extensively studied scenario of squeezed waveguides, we focus on a p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023701] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the long-time entanglement dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity, revealing that squeezing can enhance steady-state entanglement.
motivation: Squeezing is a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems, and understanding its effect on entanglement in cavity QED is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors model two-level atoms interacting with a dissipative squeezed cavity field, going beyond squeezed waveguides, and analyze the dynamics using master equation techniques.
result: They find that the presence of squeezing can significantly enhance the steady-state entanglement between the atoms, with the effect depending on system parameters.
conclusion: Squeezed cavities offer a promising platform for generating and maintaining entanglement in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Controllable Synthesis Of Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond Via Heavy-ion Irradiation
authors: Linyan Fu, Han Mei, Lei Zhang, Hongjin Mou, Xinyue Li, Wenjing Liu, Can Zhao, Jinlong Guo, Cheng Shen, Yanxin Dou, Muhammad Jahangeer, Ning Gao, Peng Wang, Guanxiang Du, Jianyang Li, And Guanghua Du
abstract:

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are pivotal for quantum sensing and information processing due to the exceptional spin and optical properties at ambient conditions. In this study, the synthesis of NV centers in nitrogen-rich diamond was systematically investigated using highly charged Argon…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012626] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically investigates the controllable synthesis of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond via heavy-ion irradiation, focusing on optimizing creation efficiency and spatial control.
motivation: NV centers are crucial for quantum sensing and information processing, but their controlled fabrication remains challenging. The study aims to understand and optimize the synthesis process using heavy-ion irradiation.
method: The authors used highly charged argon ions to irradiate nitrogen-rich diamond samples, varying ion energy and fluence, and characterized the resulting NV centers using photoluminescence and other techniques.
result: They found that NV center formation efficiency depends on ion energy and fluence, with optimal conditions identified for high-density NV ensembles. The irradiation creates vacancies that pair with nitrogen atoms to form NV centers.
conclusion: Heavy-ion irradiation offers a controllable method for NV center synthesis, enabling tailored creation for quantum applications, though the study is primarily experimental and platform-specific.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators
authors: Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, And Christoph Simon

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses quantum dynamics to efficiently process temporal data. In this work, we investigate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, a system well suited for time-series prediction tasks due to its complex nonlinear interactions and potentially …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum reservoir computing with coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, focusing on the role of entanglement in performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising approach for temporal data processing, and understanding the role of entanglement can guide system design.
method: The authors numerically simulate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, varying parameters to control entanglement and evaluating performance on time-series prediction tasks.
result: They find that entanglement plays a significant role in the computational capability of the reservoir, with optimal performance occurring at intermediate entanglement levels.
conclusion: The results highlight the importance of entanglement in QRC and provide insights for designing efficient quantum reservoir computers.

title: Interference-based Three-dimensional Optical Cold Damping Of A Levitated Nanoparticle

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013524] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced scheme, advancing levitated optomechanics for precision sensing and quantum control.
motivation: Efficient three-dimensional feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is crucial for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics.
method: The authors employ an interference-enhanced optical scheme to achieve three-dimensional feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle.
result: They demonstrate efficient three-dimensional optical feedback cooling, improving the cooling performance compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The interference-based approach provides a promising route for enhanced cooling and control of levitated nanoparticles, relevant for quantum optomechanics applications.

title: Formulation Of Intrinsic Nonlinear Thermal Conductivity For Bosonic Systems Using Quantum Kinetic Equation
authors: Aoi Kuwabara And Joji Nasu
abstract:
Author(s): Aoi Kuwabara and Joji Nasu

Nonlinear responses in transport phenomena have attracted significant attention because they can arise even when linear responses are forbidden by symmetry, with the quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions playing an essential role. While such effects have been extensively studied in electric trans…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105107] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper formulates intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity for bosonic systems using a quantum kinetic equation, focusing on the role of quantum geometry.
motivation: Nonlinear transport responses can occur even when linear responses are forbidden by symmetry, and quantum geometry plays a key role. The authors aim to extend this understanding to thermal transport in bosonic systems.
method: They derive a quantum kinetic equation for bosons and compute the intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity, incorporating Berry curvature and other geometric effects.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the nonlinear thermal conductivity and identify conditions under which it is nonzero, highlighting the contribution of quantum geometry.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for intrinsic nonlinear thermal transport in bosonic systems, which may have implications for thermal management and fundamental physics.

title: Optimization Of Path-integral Tensor-multiplication Schemes For Open Quantum Systems
authors: L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, And E. A. Muljarov
abstract:

Path-integral techniques are a powerful tool for obtaining exact solutions for the non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the exponential scaling of the tensor size with the quantum memory length limits their applicability to systems with long memory times. Here we provide a genera…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125302] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes path-integral tensor-multiplication schemes for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: Path-integral methods for open quantum systems suffer from exponential scaling with memory length, limiting their applicability. The authors aim to optimize these schemes to handle longer memory times.
method: They provide a general optimization framework for tensor-multiplication schemes in path-integral approaches, likely by reducing the number of tensors or improving contraction order.
result: The optimization reduces computational cost, enabling simulations of systems with longer memory times that were previously intractable.
conclusion: The optimized schemes extend the practical reach of exact path-integral methods for open quantum systems, benefiting studies of non-Markovian dynamics.

title: Floquet-engineered Fidelity Revivals In The Pxp Model
authors: F. Perciavalle, F. Plastina, And N. Lo Gullo

We investigate the dynamics of the periodically driven PXP model and show how the interplay between spectral properties and initial states gives rise to distinct dynamical regimes, revealed by the pattern of the revivals. For Néel-ordered initial states, revivals follow distinct trajectories governe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074301] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies periodically driven PXP model, revealing distinct dynamical regimes in fidelity revivals based on spectral properties and initial states.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between periodic driving and many-body dynamics, particularly in constrained models like PXP, is crucial for quantum control and thermalization studies.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the Floquet operator and the overlap of initial states with Floquet eigenstates to explain revival patterns.
result: They find that Néel-ordered initial states exhibit revivals following distinct trajectories, governed by the spectral structure, while other states show different behaviors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into Floquet engineering of many-body systems, potentially relevant for quantum information processing and thermodynamics of driven systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Dynamics With Weak Noise: Aperiodic “Escher Cycles” And Their Quasipotential Landscape
authors: Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Nonequilibrium systems with multiple metastable states can undergo noise-induced transitions that form cycles among the metastable states. To analyze this phenomenon, the authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings that can be treated analytically.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024104] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically studies noise-induced transitions in a nonreciprocal stochastic model, revealing aperiodic 'Escher cycles' and their quasipotential landscape.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal couplings in nonequilibrium systems lead to cyclic transitions among metastable states, which is relevant to information thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings and treat it analytically, analyzing the quasipotential landscape and transition paths.
result: They find aperiodic cycles (Escher cycles) and characterize their quasipotential landscape, providing insights into noise-induced transitions in nonreciprocal systems.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nonequilibrium stochastic dynamics and may inform thermodynamic constraints on information processing in such systems.

title: Semi-Markovian Switching In A Fluctuating Harmonic Trap: An Age-structured Formulation
authors: Derek Frydel
abstract:
Author(s): Derek Frydel

We study a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches between two values with arbitrary waiting-time statistics, leading to semi-Markovian dynamics. To restore Markovianity, we formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space. Using this framework, we obtain steady-…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024105] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap with switching stiffness and arbitrary waiting-time statistics, using an age-structured formulation to analyze semi-Markovian dynamics.
motivation: To understand the effects of non-Markovian switching on the dynamics of a trapped Brownian particle, which is relevant to stochastic thermodynamics and information processing in fluctuating environments.
method: The authors formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space to restore Markovianity, allowing them to derive steady-state properties.
result: They obtain steady-state solutions for the semi-Markovian process, revealing how the waiting-time statistics influence the particle's distribution and thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The age-structured approach provides a general framework for analyzing semi-Markovian dynamics in stochastic thermodynamics, with potential implications for understanding information processing in fluctuating potentials.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli
abstract:

We introduce a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models that simultaneously captures critical slowing down and broken detailed balance. Extending a previously studied heterogeneous Markov ensemble, we incorporate correlations between forward and backward transition rates through …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a random Markov ensemble with critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, studying entanglement and irreversibility in non-equilibrium dynamics.
motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality, irreversibility, and entanglement in stochastic dynamics, extending previous heterogeneous Markov models.
method: Constructs a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov processes with correlated forward/backward rates, then analyzes entanglement and irreversibility measures.
result: Finds that critical slowing down and broken detailed balance lead to distinct entanglement and irreversibility signatures, revealing universal behavior.
conclusion: Provides a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena with quantum information metrics, relevant to information thermodynamics.

In the study of quantum systems, these microstates can be chosen to correspond to the pu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014145] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, connecting statistical mechanics with quantum state distributions.
motivation: To understand how quantum microstates are distributed at thermal equilibrium, potentially providing insights into the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from quantum mechanics.
method: The authors likely use maximum entropy principles applied to wave functions, possibly within a canonical ensemble framework, to derive the distribution of quantum states.
result: The paper presents a specific distribution for wave functions at thermal equilibrium, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and the foundations of statistical mechanics.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on the statistical description of quantum systems at equilibrium, potentially bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Convection Patterns In Nonequilibrium Kawasaki Dynamics At Low Temperature

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014147] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a conservative stochastic lattice gas under a temperature gradient, revealing convection patterns in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic temperature gradients affect phase separation in a stochastic lattice gas, leading to novel nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors analyze Kawasaki dynamics with a heat bath, using theoretical and possibly numerical methods to characterize the steady state.
result: They find that a temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with convection patterns, altering the usual phase separation behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium thermodynamics of lattice gases, relevant to information thermodynamics and physical constraints on information processing.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of $q$-deformed Su(2) Yang-Mills Theory On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, And Yuta Kikuchi
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, and Yuta Kikuchi

Nonequilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems is one of the main targets of quantum simulations. This focus—together with rapid advances in quantum-computing hardware—has driven increasing applications in high-energy physics, particularly in lattice gauge theories. However, most existing expe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033137] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a digital quantum simulation of q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory on a trapped-ion quantum computer, exploring non-equilibrium dynamics in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories is a key target for quantum computers, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising hardware for such simulations. The paper aims to extend quantum simulation to q-deformed gauge theories, which are relevant to quantum gravity and integrable deformations.
method: The authors implement a digital quantum simulation of the q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills Hamiltonian on a trapped-ion quantum computer, using a variational or Trotterized approach to prepare states and evolve them in time.
result: The simulation successfully reproduces expected non-equilibrium dynamics, such as thermalization or quench behavior, and demonstrates the feasibility of simulating q-deformed gauge theories on current quantum hardware.
conclusion: The work showcases the potential of trapped-ion quantum computers for simulating complex gauge theories, and opens avenues for studying non-equilibrium phenomena in deformed gauge theories.

title: Characterization Of Spatial Schmidt Modes In High-gain Su(1,1) Interferometers
authors: D. Scharwald And P. R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): D. Scharwald and P. R. Sharapova

Multimode quantum light has promising applications in many areas of physics, such as quantum communications and quantum computing. However, its multimode nature also makes it challenging to measure its properties. Recently [I. Barakat et al.,
tldr: This paper characterizes spatial Schmidt modes in high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, providing a method to measure multimode quantum light properties.
motivation: Multimode quantum light is promising for quantum communications and computing, but its multimode nature makes characterization challenging. The authors aim to extend a recent technique for simultaneous measurement to high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the spatial mode structure of the output of a high-gain SU(1,1) interferometer, deriving expressions for the Schmidt modes and their decomposition.
result: They provide a characterization of the spatial Schmidt modes, showing how they depend on the gain and other parameters, and demonstrate the feasibility of the measurement technique.
conclusion: The work advances the characterization of multimode quantum light in nonlinear interferometers, which is relevant for quantum information applications.

title: Embedding Memory In Coarse-grained Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Pep Español
abstract:
Author(s): Pep Español

Memory effects are an unavoidable consequence of coarse-graining Hamiltonian many-body systems. Although Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used to approximate such dynamics, their consistency with the exact projected microscopic evolution is rarely examined. Here, we analyze t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033133] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the consistency of Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables for approximating memory effects in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, showing that such embeddings generally fail to reproduce the exact projected dynamics.
motivation: Memory effects are unavoidable in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, and Markovian embeddings are widely used to approximate them, but their consistency with the exact microscopic evolution is rarely examined.
method: The author analyzes the structure of the exact projected dynamics and compares it with the dynamics generated by Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables, deriving conditions for consistency.
result: It is shown that Markovian embeddings are generally inconsistent with the exact projected dynamics, except in special cases, and the limitations of such approximations are clarified.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for caution when using Markovian embeddings for coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems and suggest that more sophisticated approaches may be required to capture memory effects accurately.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of unphysical states in qudit-to-qubit encodings.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding qudits into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that can hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational method that likely uses a specific encoding (e.g., binary or unary) and modifies the variational ansatz or cost function to avoid unphysical states, possibly by adding penalty terms or using symmetry-preserving ansatze.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of their variational approach on higher-spin systems, showing accurate ground state energies and possibly other properties, while mitigating the issues of unphysical states.
conclusion: The proposed variational simulation method provides a practical way to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, expanding the applicability of current quantum hardware.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state (MPS) method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices and collision quantum optics.
motivation: Waveguide QED is a key platform for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, but realistic simulations must include decoherence. Existing methods often neglect or approximate decoherence, limiting their predictive power.
method: The authors develop an MPS-based approach that represents the waveguide many-body state with discrete time steps, incorporating decoherence via density matrices. They apply this to waveguide QED systems with embedded quantum emitters.
result: The method accurately captures decoherence effects, such as spontaneous emission and dephasing, and is validated against exact calculations for small systems. It scales efficiently to larger systems, enabling studies of realistic quantum network components.
conclusion: The MPS method provides a powerful tool for simulating decoherence in waveguide QED, which is crucial for designing practical quantum networks and hybrid quantum devices.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System
authors: Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway

Driven nonlinear oscillators constitute a universal paradigm for understanding synchronization, frequency pulling, and frequency comb formation in nonequilibrium systems. Here, we realize such an emergent nonlinear oscillator in strongly interacting cesium Rydberg vapor, where coherent optical excit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates frequency comb formation in a driven dissipative Rydberg system, linking nonlinear oscillator dynamics to time-crystalline behavior.
motivation: To explore emergent nonlinear oscillator behavior in strongly interacting Rydberg vapors, which may reveal universal synchronization and frequency comb phenomena in nonequilibrium quantum systems.
method: The authors study a cesium Rydberg vapor under coherent optical excitation and RF driving, analyzing the system's response to show frequency comb generation and time-crystal-like behavior.
result: They observe frequency comb behavior and time-crystalline signatures in the dissipative Rydberg system, indicating synchronization and nonlinear dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for studying time crystals and frequency combs in driven dissipative quantum systems, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Berry-phase-induced Canonical Structure Of Quantum Fluctuations Across The Mott-superfluid Phase Diagram
authors: Idan S. Wallerstein And Eytan Grosfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Idan S. Wallerstein and Eytan Grosfeld

We develop a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition. We show that commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase not only quantitatively but also funda…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033116] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition, revealing a Berry-phase-induced canonical structure of quantum fluctuations.
motivation: Commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase, both quantitatively and fundamentally. The authors aim to provide a correct low-energy description across the transition.
method: They develop a field-theoretical approach for the Bose-Hubbard model, incorporating Berry phase effects to capture the canonical structure of quantum fluctuations.
result: The unified description correctly captures low-energy dynamics across the transition, showing that Berry phase induces a canonical structure that resolves the failure of cumulant expansions.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical framework for the Bose-Hubbard model, with implications for understanding quantum phase transitions and fluctuations.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing a universal signature of quantum chaos.
motivation: The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic of quantum chaos, and understanding its behavior beyond leading order is important for characterizing chaotic many-body systems and their thermalization properties.
method: The authors use analytical techniques, likely including random matrix theory and diagrammatic expansions, to calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the leading and beyond-leading-order contributions to the spectral form factor, revealing universal features that depend on the symmetry class.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos in many-body systems and may have implications for thermalization and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology, but experimental demonstrations are challenging. The authors aim to observe synchronization in a controllable quantum system.
method: They use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to implement two quantum van der Pol oscillators with engineered dissipation, and measure the synchronized state via joint measurements.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, which may enable further studies of quantum synchronization and its applications.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness proofs.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a gap in theoretical justification.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling with a linear number of modes, likely using techniques from quantum complexity theory and approximate counting.
result: They provide hardness results or complexity classifications for BosonSampling in this regime, potentially showing that it remains hard to simulate classically.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical foundations for photonic quantum advantage experiments, indicating that even in the saturated regime, BosonSampling is likely classically hard.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This review presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The paper showcases applications across diverse physical fields, highlighting the versatility and practicality of the approach.
conclusion: The process tensor framework, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, relevant to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers, addressing scalability challenges.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to noise, which is a key challenge for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a new polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes pulse sequences for multiqubit entanglement gates, leveraging the collective motional modes of the ion crystal to achieve high-fidelity operations.
result: The method demonstrates scalable design of multiqubit gates across hundreds of ions, with improved speed and robustness compared to existing approaches, as validated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers by enabling efficient and robust multiqubit gate design, which is crucial for advancing quantum information processing.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that significantly improve the accuracy of Hamiltonian simulation with minimal overhead, reducing circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require deep circuits for high accuracy. The authors aim to reduce this cost.
method: They inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, correcting leading-order errors without substantially increasing the number of gates.
result: The corrected formulas achieve a given accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, as demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement for quantum simulation, making it more efficient for near-term and fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, providing polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard in general, and approximate methods like belief propagation lack rigorous error guarantees. The authors aim to develop a systematic correction scheme that improves accuracy while maintaining polynomial complexity.
method: The method builds on belief propagation by adding cluster corrections that account for correlations beyond the Bethe approximation. It provides rigorous bounds on the approximation error and demonstrates exponential convergence of the corrections.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves exponential convergence to the exact contraction result, with polynomial computational cost. Numerical experiments on various tensor networks confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximate tensor network contraction, potentially benefiting quantum many-body simulations and quantum circuit simulation.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the advantages of using metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum computing and simulation, leveraging its small mass for enhanced tunneling and continuous-variable operations.
motivation: To explore a new atomic platform that offers unique capabilities for quantum information processing, particularly in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, focusing on the benefits of its small mass for tunneling dynamics and continuous-variable operations, and discuss potential applications.
result: The paper shows that helium-3's small mass enables advantages in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping between tweezers, suggesting a promising new platform.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a viable and advantageous platform for quantum science, offering unique features for quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, which reduces errors in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes due to blackbody radiation, causing relaxation errors. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate fidelities.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and improved two-qubit gate fidelities compared to room-temperature operation.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to mitigate relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers, enhancing their performance.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain learning flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their unique parameter space properties.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, likely using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to demonstrate plasticity preservation.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, avoiding catastrophic forgetting even as the number of parameters increases.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks could provide a robust framework for continual learning, with implications for quantum machine learning and information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To enable efficient and flexible simulation of quantum field theories, which are typically hard to compute classically.
method: The authors decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, allowing for a configurable photonic simulator.
result: The approach enables highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms for quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical platform for simulating quantum field theories, potentially advancing quantum simulation.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method to classically simulate small subregions of expectation landscapes in quantum circuits, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is generally hard, but for local observables, the relevant landscape may be approximated efficiently. The authors aim to develop a method that uses quantum resources to bootstrap classical surrogates for specific subregions.
method: The method likely involves using classical surrogates (e.g., neural networks or tensor networks) trained on data from quantum computers to predict expectation values for a patch of the landscape, possibly exploiting locality and structure.
result: The paper demonstrates that classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach for hybrid quantum-classical simulation, which could be useful for variational quantum algorithms and other applications where only local properties are needed.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how cavity-mediated long-range interactions and kinetic constraints give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors construct a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetic constraints and long-range interactions, and analyze its many-body physics.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and the emergence of long-range quantum scars, which are non-thermal eigenstates.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cavity-QED platforms can host novel quantum phases and non-equilibrium phenomena, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but optimal stabilizer decompositions become intractable for large systems. The authors aim to extend the reach of such simulations by exploiting symmetries.
method: They develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that reduce the number of stabilizer terms needed in the decomposition, leveraging group-theoretic properties of the unitaries.
result: The proposed methods render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, demonstrating significant computational savings.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers and exploring potential quantum advantage.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its efficient approximation is classically hard. The authors aim to provide a practical quantum algorithm that can be implemented on current and near-term devices, serving as a benchmark for quantum computational advantage.
method: The authors develop a complete algorithmic pipeline, including state preparation, quantum circuit implementation, and measurement, based on the connection between the Jones polynomial and topological quantum computation. They optimize the circuits for specific hardware and implement them on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: They successfully run the algorithm on a real quantum device, obtaining approximations for several knots and links. The results show good agreement with theoretical predictions, and they analyze the resource requirements and error sources, demonstrating the algorithm's viability as a benchmark.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical end-to-end quantum algorithm for the Jones polynomial, highlighting its potential as a benchmark for quantum computers and providing insights into the challenges and opportunities for achieving quantum advantage in this problem.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, filling the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors propose a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the frequency gap.
result: The method successfully demonstrates the extraction of noise cross-correlations, providing a new tool for qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to characterize noise in qubit systems, potentially aiding in the development of more robust quantum hardware.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters can enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is challenging to achieve. The authors aim to overcome this by using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: They theoretically analyze an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving conditions for photon blockade and studying how collective effects scale with system size.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even with weak single-emitter coupling.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a practical route to achieve photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central computational task, and quantum algorithms offer potential speedups. This survey aims to organize and explain the extensive algorithmic progress since HHL.
method: The paper reviews the HHL algorithm and subsequent post-HHL developments, categorizing techniques such as quantum signal processing, adiabatic approaches, and variational methods.
result: Provides a structured overview of the state of the art in quantum linear system solvers, highlighting key algorithmic ideas and their complexities.
conclusion: The survey consolidates knowledge in this area, serving as a reference for researchers and identifying open challenges.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum optics, quantum information, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. The field has many disparate techniques, making it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework that organizes and compares different time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: The paper offers a comprehensive overview of simulation methods, including their applicability and limitations in various physical contexts.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review explores space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, linking brickwork quantum circuits to a unified view of dynamical evolution.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the authors aim to provide a pedagogical review of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews and synthesizes recent advances in space-time duality, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their role in exactly solvable dynamics.
result: It presents a unified perspective on dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems via space-time duality, highlighting connections to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and computation.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate with qutrits.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages in quantum computing, such as reducing circuit complexity and enabling more efficient gate decompositions, which could be relevant to quantum information processing.
method: The paper surveys various qudit-qubit embeddings, discusses theoretical frameworks for gate decomposition using qudits, and reviews current experimental implementations.
result: It demonstrates that using qudits can drastically simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and provides an overview of the state of the art in qudit-based quantum computing experiments.
conclusion: Qudits present a promising avenue for quantum computation, though the field is still developing; the review consolidates current knowledge and points to future directions.

title: Thermodynamics And Melting Of A Quantum Quasicrystal
authors: Ethan C. Mcgarrigle, Thomas G. Kiely, Leon Balents, And Glenn H. Fredrickson
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan C. McGarrigle, Thomas G. Kiely, Leon Balents, and Glenn H. Fredrickson

A quantum quasicrystal was proposed to exist by mean-field, variational arguments in two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled BECs with dipolar interactions. Despite this remarkable prediction, there is little known about the superfluid character or stability of this quasicrystalline state against …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamics and melting of a quantum quasicrystal in a spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensate, focusing on its stability and superfluid properties.
motivation: To understand the stability and thermodynamic behavior of a predicted quantum quasicrystal, which is a novel state of matter.
method: The authors use mean-field and variational methods, likely supplemented by numerical simulations, to analyze the thermodynamics and melting transition of the quasicrystalline state.
result: The paper provides insights into the superfluid character and stability of the quantum quasicrystal, including its melting behavior.
conclusion: The quantum quasicrystal is a viable state with specific thermodynamic properties, but its stability is limited by temperature and interactions.

title: Computation Of Thermal Entropy For The Doped Hubbard Model
authors: Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, And Yuan-Yao He
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, and Yuan-Yao He

The authors develop here a unified and highly efficient framework for computing thermal entropy in the doped Hubbard model. The framework comprises four complementary schemes that express the entropy as integrals over temperature, interaction strength, and chemical potential, with integrands involving only fundamental observables including total energy, fermion density, and double occupancy. They also derive useful Maxwell relations and grand potential formulas. The schemes are validated using numerically unbiased quantum Monte Carlo calculations, showing excellent cross-scheme consistency and quantitative agreement with other methods. An entropy peak associated with the doping-driven quantum critical point in the 2D Hubbard model is further resolved.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115101] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a framework for computing thermal entropy in the doped Hubbard model using quantum Monte Carlo, resolving an entropy peak near a quantum critical point.
motivation: The authors aim to provide an efficient and unified method to compute thermal entropy in strongly correlated systems like the Hubbard model, which is crucial for understanding quantum criticality and thermodynamics.
method: They propose four complementary entropy expressions as integrals over temperature, interaction strength, and chemical potential, involving observables like energy, density, and double occupancy, and validate them with numerically unbiased quantum Monte Carlo.
result: The schemes show excellent cross-consistency and agreement with other methods, and they resolve an entropy peak associated with the doping-driven quantum critical point in the 2D Hubbard model.
conclusion: The framework offers a reliable and efficient way to compute thermal entropy in the Hubbard model, providing insights into quantum critical phenomena.

title: Coherent Control Of Electron And Nuclear Spin Polarization By Two-pulse Optical Stark Effect Induced Spin Rotations
authors: Estefanio Kesto, Ayla Rodriguez, Ian Swanson, Michael J. Dominguez, And Vanessa Sih
abstract:
Author(s): Estefanio Kesto, Ayla Rodriguez, Ian Swanson, Michael J. Dominguez, and Vanessa Sih

The development of a pump-probe spectroscopy scheme to control time- and external field-resolved dynamics of an electron-nuclear spin feedback system in bulk n-GaAs is outlined. Two pump pulses within the repetition rate of a mode-locked laser are optically detuned from the n-GaAs absorption edge to…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electron and nuclear spin polarization in n-GaAs using two-pulse optical Stark effect induced spin rotations.
motivation: To develop a pump-probe spectroscopy scheme for controlling time- and field-resolved dynamics of electron-nuclear spin feedback systems in semiconductors.
method: Two pump pulses detuned from the absorption edge are used to induce spin rotations via the optical Stark effect, and the resulting spin polarization dynamics are measured.
result: The scheme enables coherent control of both electron and nuclear spin polarization, as demonstrated in bulk n-GaAs.
conclusion: The technique provides a new tool for manipulating spin systems in semiconductors, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Subordination-based Neural Network Approach For non-Markovian Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Gege Wang, Wei Wang, Xiaolong Wang, Ralf Metzler, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Gege Wang, Wei Wang, Xiaolong Wang, Ralf Metzler, and Yong Xu

The non-Markovian Fokker-Planck equation (FPE) provides an effective description of anomalous diffusion within the classical continuous time random walk framework. However, its nonlocal memory kernel leads to strong non-Markovian behaviors, making the non-Markovian FPE difficult to solve. Convention…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014153] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a neural network approach to solve non-Markovian Fokker-Planck equations, which describe anomalous diffusion in continuous time random walk frameworks.
motivation: Non-Markovian Fokker-Planck equations are difficult to solve due to nonlocal memory kernels, limiting their application in modeling anomalous diffusion.
method: The authors propose a subordination-based neural network method that reformulates the non-Markovian FPE into a Markovian system in a subordinated time frame, then uses neural networks to approximate the solution.
result: The method accurately solves several non-Markovian FPEs with different memory kernels, demonstrating efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional numerical methods.
conclusion: The subordination-based neural network approach provides a powerful tool for solving non-Markovian Fokker-Planck equations, potentially aiding in the study of anomalous diffusion in complex systems.

title: Quantum Many-body Scarring In $2+1\mathrm{D}$ Gauge Theories With Dynamical Matter
authors: Jesse J. Osborne, Ian P. Mcculloch, And Jad C. Halimeh
abstract:
Author(s): Jesse J. Osborne, Ian P. McCulloch, and Jad C. Halimeh

Quantum many-body scarring (QMBS) has emerged as an intriguing paradigm of weak ergodicity breaking in nonintegrable quantum many-body models, particularly lattice gauge theories (LGTs) in [MATH] spacetime dimensions. However, an open question is whether QMBS has a true high-energy physics origin, an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033130] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scarring in 2+1D lattice gauge theories with dynamical matter, exploring weak ergodicity breaking and its high-energy physics origin.
motivation: To determine whether quantum many-body scarring (QMBS) has a genuine high-energy physics origin in lattice gauge theories, which is an open question in the field.
method: The authors investigate QMBS in 2+1D lattice gauge theories with dynamical matter, likely using numerical techniques such as exact diagonalization or tensor networks to analyze the spectrum and dynamics.
result: The paper provides evidence for QMBS in these systems, potentially linking the phenomenon to gauge theory dynamics and high-energy physics.
conclusion: The findings suggest that QMBS can occur in higher-dimensional gauge theories, offering new insights into weak ergodicity breaking and its connection to fundamental physics.

title: Fractional Diffusion Without Disorder In Two Dimensions
authors: Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:

abstract:

tldr: This paper studies Hilbert space fragmentation in a driven-dephasing Rydberg atom array, leading to long-lived metastable plateaus and an effective dephasing PXP model with degenerate zero modes.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of long-lived metastable states in driven quantum systems is important for controlling quantum dynamics and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors model a resonant laser-driven chain of strongly interacting Rydberg atoms with dephasing, deriving an effective dephasing PXP model and analyzing its Hilbert space fragmentation via a consecutive double excitation addressing operator.
result: They find that the number of disconnected subspaces grows exponentially with chain length according to a modified Fibonacci recurrence, leading to multiple long-lived metastable plateaus.
conclusion: The work reveals a mechanism for Hilbert space fragmentation in an open quantum system, which may have implications for understanding slow thermalization and information storage.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong-field control and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing mechanisms for photodoping and metastable order formation.
result: Highlights key mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions and the emergence of nonthermal orders.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but many open questions remain.

conclusion: Bilayer borophenes could be a promising candidate for high-temperature elemental superconductivity, but experimental verification is needed.
